Flavor_Text: A senior spots you at MT looking entirely burnt out and buys you a cold coffee. Hearing "everyone fails this course" drops your stress instantly.
You overslept for an 8 AM lecture, but a wingmate clutched the proxy. You save time, but completely miss the core concepts.
The wing decides to pirate a movie at 2 AM. You sacrifice your sleep and study plans for pure, unadulterated bonding.
You find someone in the PKK Library who actually understands the assignment. A highly productive, collaborative session ensues.
Midnight hunger strikes. You spend your limited cash on a Maggi break at the Hall Canteen to preserve your sanity.
Your secondhand cycle betrays you on the way to LHC. You waste precious time dragging it to the repair shop.
The campus weather shifts and the "IITK cough" gets you. You are bedridden and lose critical momentum.
The washing machines are full, and someone dumped your wet clothes out. You waste time sorting out the hostel chaos.
The mess food is entirely inedible today. You either starve or spend your limited cash eating at the food court.
Panic sets in at the library gate. Your ID is gone. You spend hours navigating the DOAA office to get a replacement.
You receive the dreaded "short attendance" warning email. You must spend extra blocks begging the professor or face an automatic grade drop.
Three different deadlines hit on the exact same day. You are forced into an all-nighter, completely sacrificing your health and social life.
The hostel loses power in the middle of summer. Study efficiency plummets, but the whole wing gathers outside to complain, bonding in the heat.
Ping! Course allotment goes perfectly. You have no 8 AM classes and get a "god schedule," putting you in a fantastic mental state for the semester.
You draw the lottery: the professor for your heaviest core course is surprisingly chill and doesn't care about strict deadlines.
The first quiz for your core department course hits. You realize "First Class Honours" isn't a guarantee here. The academic anxiety spikes.
You manage to join a study group with the batch toppers. The imposter syndrome is real, but your understanding of the material skyrockets.
You ignored one assignment, and now it has snowballed into three. You have to lock yourself in the CC and grind just to break even.
A massive post-midsem celebration goes too long. You wake up feeling terrible, having completely destroyed your momentum for the next day.
You walk out of the exam hall feeling light as a feather. The questions matched what you actually studied. Pure relief washes over you.
After weeks of staring at the textbook, the abstract math finally clicks in your head. You feel like a genius for exactly five minutes.
You sit down in the examination hall, look at Question 1, and your mind completely blanks. The creeping dread of a failing grade sets in.
The code compiles. The error is gone. Everything finally works. You sink a massive amount of time into refining it, but the payoff is huge.
